# Animation

Plays one skeletal clip on the SkinnedMeshRenderer of the same object (Unity: Animation).

Availability: **PSX** no | **PSP** yes | **PS2** yes

The component or type needs the `skinning` feature (skeletal animation (psx uses segmented rigid models)). If it is missing: use sprite or vertex animation.

Time is a whole number of fixed steps, so a clip plays the same on every profile. Skinning matrices are computed in the animation system, once per fixed step, and shared by every draw.

## Members

| Member | PSX | PSP | PS2 | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Guid clip` | no | yes | yes | The glTF asset; its first animation is played. |
| `bool playAutomatically` | no | yes | yes | Starts when the scene loads. |
| `int wrapMode` | no | yes | yes | 0 = the clip's own loop flag, 1 = once, 2 = loop. |
| `Scalar speed` | no | yes | yes | 1 = normal. |
| `void Play()` | no | yes | yes | Restarts the clip from its first frame. |
| `void Stop()` | no | yes | yes | Stops and keeps the pose. |
| `bool isPlaying() const` | no | yes | yes | False after a one-shot clip ends. |

## Limits

| Limit | PSX | PSP | PS2 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Skinned joints per skeleton (0 = none) | 0 | 64 | 64 |

## Notes

- `Play()` and `Stop()` fail to compile on a profile without `skinning`, with a hint.
- Switching between clips: put each clip on its own object, or restart with `Play()`. Blending is not part of F5.

## Example

```cpp
Animation* a = GetComponent<Animation>();
if (moving && !a->isPlaying()) a->Play();
if (!moving && a->isPlaying()) a->Stop();
```

See also: [API availability by profile](../api-availability.md), [API index](index.md).
